div.p: Match each flower part label to its correct location on the diagram.
Click and hold a label from the word bank at the bottom, then drag it to the matching location on the flower.
Use the buttons below to get hints, check your answers, or reset the activity.
Hover over parts of the flower to see their names.

div.style: font-family: 'Segoe UI', Tahoma, Geneva, Verdana, sans-serif; font-size: 22px; color: #34495e; line-height: 1.8; padding: 20px;
div.p: Petal: Brightly colored parts that attract pollinators
Sepal: Green leaf-like structures that protect the bud
Stamen: The male reproductive part (consists of anther and filament)
Pistil: The female reproductive part (consists of stigma, style, and ovary)
Anther: Produces pollen at the top of the stamen
Filament: The stalk that supports the anther
Ovary: Contains ovules that develop into seeds after fertilization
Style: The stalk connecting stigma to ovary
Stigma: Sticky surface that receives pollen
Receptacle: The base where all flower parts attach
Look at the shape and position of each part. Petals are colorful and prominent, while sepals are green and protective. Stamens surround the central pistil.

div.style: font-family: 'Segoe UI', Tahoma, Geneva, Verdana, sans-serif; font-size: 24px; color: #2c3e50; line-height: 2.0; padding: 20px;
div.p: A. Petal - The colorful parts that attract pollinators
B. Sepal - Green protective structures around the bud
C. Stamen - Male reproductive organ (anther + filament)
D. Pistil - Female reproductive organ (stigma + style + ovary)
E. Anther - Pollen-producing part of the stamen
F. Filament - Stalk supporting the anther
G. Ovary - Base of pistil containing ovules
H. Style - Stalk connecting stigma to ovary
I. Stigma - Sticky tip that receives pollen
J. Receptacle - Base where all parts attach to the stem
Great job learning flower anatomy! Understanding these parts helps explain how plants reproduce.

Tip: Start with the most distinctive parts like petals and sepals,
then move to the reproductive structures in the center.
